clue.text: Like some beaks, red in a tipsy outbreak

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: describing certain magistrates

indicators.note: an outbreak is a wild eruption, so these letters break out into a new order

explanation.surface: Magistrates who turn red when a drunk causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaks' is British slang for magistrates; a stipendiary magistrate is a paid, legally qualified one. 'outbreak' rearranges RED IN A TIPSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid professional magistrates in Britain were called stipendiary, as opposed to unpaid lay justices.

clue.text: It will shrink the cloth

indicators.note: to shrink is to get smaller, so only part of the phrase is kept, the letters running across both words

explanation.surface: A warning that washing will make the fabric shrink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' trims the phrase IT WILL by its opening letter, so the cloth sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a fabric woven with diagonal parallel ribs.

clue.text: Coppers take in a name for punishment

indicators.note: to take in is to hold inside, so the coins enclose the other letters

parts.note: copper coins are pennies, PENCE

explanation.surface: Police officers detain someone by name as a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police but means copper coins, pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-imposed suffering done to atone for a wrong.

clue.text: Ether or three possibly

definitions.meaning: ether is an anaesthetic, something that numbs
three is an example of a figure

explanation.surface: Puzzling over whether something is ether or the figure three.
explanation.walkthrough: Read NUMBER as NUMB-ER: something that numbs, which ether does.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether deadens feeling, making it a numbing agent; three is an integer, an example of a figure.

clue.text: Abuse of nearly all litter that is spread about

indicators.note: spread about means scattered, so these letters are rearranged
nearly says the word falls just short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Mistreating things by scattering rubbish everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all' gives AL; with LITTER that is LITTERAL, which 'spread about' rearranges. 'that is' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse someone is to treat them cruelly or badly.

clue.text: Young rambler?

parts.note: a rambler is a climbing plant as well as a walker; a young one of the plant is an unopened flower

explanation.surface: A youthful hiker out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: A rambling rose is a climbing variety, so its young flower is the bud.
explanation.definitionFit: An unopened flower of a climbing plant of that kind is its young form.

clue.text: Free-lance cricket-club, even so is getting better

indicators.note: free means loose or released, so these letters are set loose into a new arrangement

parts.note: CC is the usual abbreviation for cricket club

explanation.surface: A freelance cricket club is improving after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'Free-lance' is split: its first half signals the anagram and its second half is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Convalescence is the period of recovery after illness.

clue.text: What a disappointment, loss of wealth and status

definitions.meaning: a letdown, something worse than expected
a fall in social standing and fortune

explanation.surface: Lamenting a fall from riches and position.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is both an anticlimax and a decline in rank or fortune.

clue.text: Backing group in early European song contest?

definitions.text: Backing group in early European song contest?

parts.words: Backing group in early European song contest?
parts.note: the clue suggests modern pop backing singers, but means a guild of medieval German singing poets who held contests

explanation.surface: A support band at an old Eurovision-style competition.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's opera about a singing contest among the German guild of master singers is the reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of medieval and Renaissance German poet-musician guilds competed in formal song contests.

clue.text: Return of foreign black hole in this constellation?

parts.note: a hole is round like the letter O

indicators.note: a return sends something back, so the French word is read backwards

parts.note: noir is French for black

explanation.surface: A black hole reappearing within a star group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' asks for the French word; 'Return of' reads it backwards and it follows the hole's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is the hunter figure among the stars, visible worldwide.

clue.text: Real burden, this cervical impediment

definitions.meaning: cervical means of the neck: something weighing round one's neck

explanation.surface: A heavy load that hangs around one's neck.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is a millstone around one's neck; 'cervical' refers to the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A grinding stone hung round the neck is the proverbial heavy encumbrance.

clue.text: Spontaneously growing soldier?

definitions.meaning: a plant that comes up without being sown

explanation.surface: A soldier who sprang up of their own accord.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners call a self-sown plant this; it is also an unconscripted serviceman.

clue.text: Makes infusion for contusion, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is recognised by how it is spoken

parts.note: a contusion is a bruise

explanation.surface: Making a herbal remedy to treat a bruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says BRUISE sounds like the word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To brew is to steep something, like tea, in hot water.

clue.text: Did he work in endless sterile turmoil?

definitions.text: Did he work in endless sterile turmoil?

indicators.note: turmoil is confusion, so the letters are jumbled
endless says the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Asking whether a surgeon toiled in chaotic germ-free conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes STERILE to STERIL, and 'turmoil' rearranges it; the whole clue describes the pioneer of antiseptic surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister introduced antiseptic methods, making operating conditions sterile.

clue.text: Home counties bowman is a hunter

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
a bowman shoots with a bow: an archer

explanation.surface: An archer from around London who goes hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks for something is one who hunts for it.

clue.text: Liberal worker with divers

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
divers is an old word for several, some

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician working alongside scuba divers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is not swimmers but the archaic adjective meaning various.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome sum is a generous one, so the word can mean bountiful.

clue.text: Lighter takes a long time-tears for it are in vain

definitions.text: tears for it are in vain

parts.note: a spill is a thin strip of wood or paper for lighting fires
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A lighter takes ages, and crying over it is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition echoes the proverb: no use crying over spilt milk.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says weeping over a liquid knocked over achieves nothing.

clue.text: Work of Turner's depicting a steamship in peace, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Turner painting shows a steamer in calm waters.
explanation.walkthrough: J.M.W. Turner painted many marine views; 'perhaps' rearranges A, SS and PEACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Turner is famous for paintings of the sea and ships, marine pictures.

clue.text: Support for leg is a sort of replica

indicators.note: a sort of suggests a version of the word, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A leg brace that is a kind of copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' rearranges REPLICA.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal brace strapped to a weak leg supports it.

clue.text: Who's a pretty boy, then, in Oxbridge

definitions.text: Who's a pretty boy, then, in Oxbridge

parts.words: Who's a pretty boy, then, in Oxbridge
parts.note: split into three words, it answers the question of who is in Oxbridge: a university fellow is

explanation.surface: Someone cooing at a parrot, or asking who the handsome student is at an old university.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A DON IS: a don is who is at Oxford or Cambridge; the whole is the beautiful youth of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this youth was loved by Aphrodite for his beauty, so the name means a handsome young man.

clue.text: Soldier on square face about in a sort of display

indicators.note: about means around, so the clock face surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the soldier comes before the square

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
a T-square is a drawing tool, giving T

explanation.surface: A soldier in the square with a clock face showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' stacks the soldier over the square in this down clue; 'about' wraps the clock face round both.
explanation.definitionFit: A readout showing figures rather than hands is a numeric one.

clue.text: Get stuck in gear

definitions.meaning: to set about a task with energy

explanation.surface: An instruction to start working, with equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a job is to tackle it vigorously; fishing equipment is called tackle.

clue.text: Caesar's forty said to be superior

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the letters are read by their sound

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor's forty soldiers were thought the best.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken as two letters, the Roman numeral for forty sounds like a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo others.

clue.text: Feel anger about chlorophyll

definitions.note: a noun standing for the colour it gives plants

indicators.note: about means around and in disorder, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Getting angry about plant pigment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges FEEL ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Chlorophyll is the pigment that makes foliage green, and the colour name derives from it.

clue.text: And this, in Rome, a moral principle

parts.note: et is Latin for and, the language of Rome
hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: A Roman's and this, forming a moral code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Rome' tells the solver to use Latin for both words.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a rule of right conduct.

clue.text: Reasonable chap, the hawker

parts.note: reasonably priced means inexpensive, cheap
jack is a general word for a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: A fair-minded fellow selling goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapjack was a street seller of cheap goods.

clue.text: Sound of merriment some members of debate heeded

indicators.note: some members of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: MPs in a debate laughing at what was listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans DEBATE and HEEDED.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee-hee is a giggle or titter.

clue.text: Simple task to bar building unit

parts.note: an easy job is a breeze
to block is to bar the way

explanation.surface: An easy job to obstruct construction.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightweight concrete brick made with cinders is used in construction.
